name: PrimRObject::Prim1A (SimAntics opcode 0x1a)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Two object ids A and B (operand reads, param byte +6/word +7 and byte +9/word +0xa) are resolved by param byte +5: bit 1 through the context's slot-10 manager (slot 16, error 0x1c; slot 19 hands them back), bit 3 through this's table (slot 63 -> slot 29, error 0x17, slot 109), otherwise both through the table and, when both report state 2 (slot 98), via each one's slot-61 owner (slot 28) and the manager (slot 17) to new ids (slot 8) and the target (slot 12). The target (error 0x68 when none) is asked for the count at B (slot 5): above param byte +4 stores slot 9's value into the SimDataRef operand at byte +0xc/word +0xd (error 0x13 without storage, 0x14 out of range; bit 2: slot 10 instead) and returns 1; otherwise returns 0 after a slot-6 raise to byte+4+1 (unless bit 0). Slots 47 etc. checked against the disassembly (the decompiler's argument lists on some slots belong to later calls). Differential: 40,000 seeds against recording fakes (call trace with arguments, result, thrown code, data cell), exception injection at random calls. Mutants killed (10): limit+1, error 0x13, bit-0 test, count compare, range compare, lookup id, release argument, state test, new id, error 0x17. ORIGINAL-BUG: the manager path leaks the found object when only one of the two lookups succeeds.

name: PrimRObject::Prim1C (SimAntics opcode 0x1c, looks like run-tree-by-name)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Frame slot 18 == 1 returns this's secondary slot 29 != 0. Otherwise loads a string (string-table loader, cTSString::Construct 0x1d0df0, group 0x12f, id from param byte +8 | 0x100 under word bit 6, key per bits 0/1), trims trailing blanks (verified cRZString helper), picks the objects by param byte +9 (registry at this+0x1c4 numbered by frame slot 12, its slot 280 and 89; mode 3 via this's slot-19 words and the holder's slot 14; errors 0x15, 0x7a, 0x2c), asks the tree object (slot 31) for the tree id, collects up to 4 argument words (frame slots 26/30 or three operand reads) and starts it through the caller's interface 0x99c7f5a (modes 0/1: slot 47 getters, interface slot 15 with eight arguments) or this's slots 247/248; returns 3 when started. In the test 0x1d0df0 (reaches the string-table resources) is redirected in the mapped image to a stand-in building the same 0x34-byte object from a scripted text; the real loader is not exercised. The two flag arguments of slot 31 are pushed as dwords of which the original sets only the low byte: the test compares the low byte, ours passes 0/1. 60,000 seeds; mutants killed (13): string id bit, argument pointer, error 0x2c, caller choice, flag bit, argument count, trim, early-out, word order, early-out sense, getter object, string key slot, mode check. ORIGINAL-BUG: the interface query's answer is ignored (null dereference without it).

name: PrimRObject::Prim12 (SimAntics opcode 0x12, looks like delete-object)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Param word +4 (0..2, error 9) gives the id (this's slot 47, frame slot 12, 0); the object comes from the context's table (none: 0). Objects whose type id (slot 61 -> slot 28) is in a function-local hash set at 0x10dbf54 (guard 0x10dbf74, seven ids filled on first use; the set's operations are the original's instantiations) are left alone (0). Otherwise position read (slot 41), manager told (slot 18), objects with slot 116 true go through 0x5416a0, the developer log (context slot 31; 'OETreeDelete.xls' next to the folder CommonImplSlot4 gives, written through the 0x1b4dd2 text stream and four Sprintf lines) is written, an object with interface 0x5a69d3d5 is handed to the holder's slot 29, and the result is 2 when the id is this object's own and its interface 0x99c7f5a says so with param byte +6 bit 0 clear, else 1. Differential: 40,000 seeds, the set rebuilt before every run (empty and filled), thread-safe-statics state arranged as in the Prim30 test, 0x5416a0 and the log stream functions redirected to logging stand-ins, the application forwarder through its cache global; compares trace, result and thrown code. Mutants killed (12): bit inversion, state test, mode bound, found test, slot-116 test, type table, log argument (two), interface test, manager flag, filled-set test, self test. ORIGINAL-BUG: the 0x99c7f5a query's answer is not checked.

name: PrimRObject::Prim0D (SimAntics opcode 0x0d, looks like push-interaction)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Caller person = frame slot 12 object (0x15), state 2 and interface 0x5a69d3d5 required (0x1c); target object from a frame cell, the interface's slot 10 or an argument (0x33, 8, 0x17), interaction index from an operand, the caller's slot 13 or param byte +4 (target slot 87 list, 0x1f, 0x16), priority from param byte +6 (own interface slot 10 / 100 / 20 / 50, else 0x2d); builds the original's cEdithObjectTestSim and asks the director's service 0xfc5ecc3d to take the interaction (slots 8, 46, 27, ...), refusal reasons 1..6 are stored through this's slot 14(0x34, reason) and the result is 0, success is the caller interface's slot 122 (1). In the test the test-sim ctor/dtor/two methods are redirected to logging stand-ins and the director singleton is set up as in the Prim30 test. 60,000 seeds, mutants killed (13): priority 20/100, reason codes 4 and 6, frame bound, index source, argument count, error 0x1f, data cell, getter order, stale-argument slot, notifier bit. The first argument of the owner's slot 63 is a dword of which the original sets the low byte (upper bytes: the target pointer); ours reproduces it, the test compares the low byte. ORIGINAL-BUG: the last own-interface query's answer is not checked. Lane AD: the test sim is ours; the owner's slot 63 takes no arguments and the runner takes six (the old three-argument calls only worked because the extra pushes stayed on the stack). The test runs the real sim over the handler's fakes (check-tree world mapped onto existing fakes).

name: PrimRObject::Prim0E (SimAntics opcode 0x0e, looks like find-best-object-for-function)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Param word +4 (the kind; 0..0x1b with gaps, others return 0) gives the object function and a rating cell. The registry (this+0x1c4) slot 32 returns the list of objects for that function; each is filtered (slot 25, cells 0x38/0x6b/0x19, the allowed-number set the own interface fills, slots 129/190/135), rated through this's cell 0x42 (slots 14/13), checked by the secondary slot 15 (eight arguments) and selected by param bits; the score is rating / (distance/5 + 1) weighted by the own interface's slots 79/78; the best (and, with byte +6 bit 4, one the position service accepts) wins; its number goes to the frame's slot 13 (result 1). Differential: the iterator helpers (std::list-like, 0x5a98e0 etc.) run for real on a list in static memory; the allowed-number set is library code on both sides (the original's ctor 0x57c3d0, find 0x55db30, frees 0x38eef0/0x1fcdb0 run for real; ours is a std::unordered_set<int32_t> with GameAllocator), and the own-interface stand-in fills it on both sides with the game's insert 0x420bd0 (up to 14 numbers, so the game's rehash 0x42d860 frees the first bucket vector), all under svcfx::AllocatorScope: a set of ours on another heap fails (lane WE; the std::allocator set crashed smoke b49f2793 in GeneralAllocator::FreeInternal under the game's rehash), the position-vector helpers and the two service getters are redirected to stand-ins; 60,000 seeds incl. NaN/inf distances. Mutants killed (13 of 14; the survivor, number zero- vs sign-extended, is equivalent: only its low 16 bits are ever compared): cell table, score compare, score formula (three), error 0x6d, set test (two), flag tests, selection tests. One float detail not testable here: the original multiplies the second opinion value (st0 straight from the callee) in x87 without rounding it to float first. When an error unwinds the frame the original frees only the list block of the allowed-number set (the bucket vector is leaked); since lane WC ours is a std container and frees both (the leak is not reproduced; nothing observable but the leaked block).

name: PrimRObject::Prim10 (SimAntics opcode 0x10, looks like go-to / route)
notes: Hooked (not yet run in-game). Walker = frame slot 12 object (or an operand's, byte +6 bit 3; 0x15/0x17), destination this, a frame argument (bit 0; 0x33, 0x17) or a second operand; goal = destination position (default 1.0, 1.0 floor 1). Refused by the walker's slot 25 flags (0x10000/0x20000); posts a framework message (0xaf6129c0) when its slot-64 object answers 0x13; then by param byte +4: 1 stops the route (slots 188/104/175, registry slot 106); 5..8 try the waypoints of a destination list item (frame cell, operand, own list; 8, 0x1b) through the route check 0x7e8c60 (random heading start when a waypoint has none) and commit the first passing (slots 215/171/170/216); 3/4 plan one route facing the destination's heading (0x3d); the rest plan through slot 186 (a retry with a flag cleared, not for kind 2) and announce 0xaf6129b0. The routing request (0x57c890), the position conversions (0x7dcc50/0x7dcde0/0x7dd090) are inlined. Differential: 80,000 seeds; 0x7e8c60 redirected to a logging stand-in, the messages are real cRZMessage2Standard objects (vtable slots 1/2/5/12 record), the generator a real cRZRandom with equal state on both sides, the director as in the Prim30 test. Mutants killed (15): facing +2, goal floor, frame bounds, heading mask, errors, request flags, odd test, message id, heading arithmetic, kind-2 test, headings +8, stop-route argument, flag bit, random bound, table test. ORIGINAL-BUG: the trace query and the own-interface query answers are used without null checks.
